reason: The text explicitly demonstrates the Hebrew people actively expressing their views and suffering. The passage states 'וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ וַתַּ֧עַל שַׁוְעָתָ֛ם אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים' (and they cried, and their cry came up unto God), showing they openly voiced their distress. Additionally, Moses and Aaron are given explicit instruction to speak to Pharaoh and deliver God's message. There is no statement in the text discouraging the Hebrew people from expressing their views; rather, the narrative demonstrates their active expression of suffering and their cries being heard by God.
